about.title: Personal Injury Help in Salinas, California
about.longDescription: Salinas sits at the heart of Monterey County, and its streets carry a steady mix of farm trucks, commuter traffic, and neighborhood drivers. Public records for 2025, the most recent final year, list 410 injury collisions here, with 560 people hurt and 1 life lost. The corridors that show up most often in those records are N Main Street, E Market Street, E Laurel Drive, and E Boronda Road. Reports also tend to climb on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m., when the workweek lets out. If one of those numbers now includes you, the paperwork and phone calls that follow can feel heavier than the injury itself. That is where LawProactive comes in. We are a free service, not a law firm. Our role is simple: we listen to what happened and connect you with an independent personal injury attorney who handles cases in the Salinas area. You pay nothing for the connection, and the attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. California gives most people two years to file, but claims against a city or county agency can require notice in as little as six months, so it helps to talk with someone early rather than wait.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Salinas Claim

items.title: Two Years, Sometimes Six Months
items.desc: Most California injury claims must be filed within two years of the incident. If a government entity such as the City of Salinas or Monterey County is involved, a formal claim may be due in as little as six months.

items.title: Partly at Fault? You Can Still Recover
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault. Even if you share some responsibility for what happened, your recovery is reduced by your share rather than wiped out.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no ceiling on non-economic damages like pain, lost enjoyment of life, and emotional distress.

items.title: Contingency Fees, Nothing Up Front
items.desc: Attorneys in the LawProactive network work on contingency. There is no fee unless there is a recovery in your case.

items.question: Where do injury crashes in Salinas tend to happen?
items.answer: Public collision records for Salinas show the highest counts along N Main Street, E Market Street, E Laurel Drive, and E Boronda Road. In 2025, the city recorded 410 injury collisions and 560 people injured overall. These are neutral public-record figures, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with an independent personal injury attorney. We do not provide legal advice or represent you. The attorney you are connected with handles your case directly.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in Salinas?
items.answer: For most personal injury claims in California, the deadline is two years from the date of injury. Claims involving a government agency, such as a crash with a city vehicle or a fall on public property, may require a claim within six months. An attorney can confirm which deadline applies to your situation.

items.question: What if the insurance company says I was partly to blame?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault. That means being partly responsible reduces what you can recover by your percentage of fault, but it does not bar your claim entirely. An attorney can review the evidence and push back on an unfair fault assignment.

items.question: What does it cost to get connected and hire an attorney?
items.answer: The LawProactive connection is free. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so you pay no attorney fee unless there is a recovery in your case. Specific fee terms are set out in the agreement you sign with the attorney.
